note.question: What dynamically credible portfolio policy follows when an investor judges terminal wealth by a quantile rather than expected utility, and can that equilibrium explain how risky-asset shares vary with household wealth?
note.overview: The investor's time-indexed selves are explicitly treated as different players in a dynamic intrapersonal game. An equilibrium strategy must be immune to every feasible infinitesimal deviation by the current self when future selves continue the candidate strategy; the paper characterizes those equilibria under quantile objectives.

models.method: In those studies, the authors evaluate the rate of change of the objective function when the agent deviates from the intrapersonal equilibrium in an infinitesimally small period of time and then use the rate of change to characterize the intrapersonal equilibrium by the so-called extended Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman (HJB) equation.

sources.quote: Definition 1 sti­ pulates that ˆp is an intrapersonal equilibrium if, at any time t with any wealth level x that is reachable at that time under ˆp, the objective function (i.e., the quantile of the terminal wealth) becomes smaller if they choose another amount π (satisfying the portfolio constraints) to invest in the risky assets, assuming that they can only control themselves to invest π dollars in the risky assets in an infinitesimally small period of time.

components.label: Solution or estimation method
components.explanation: The authors first demonstrate time inconsistency in a two-period model, then define continuous-time intrapersonal equilibrium through infinitesimal deviations. Because quantiles do not admit the expectation tower property, they develop an infinitesimal analysis of the quantile operator, a transportation-PDE representation, stochastic quantile bounds, and asymptotic matching to solve the equilibrium equation within affine strategies. The theoretical solution is then mapped to SCF household portfolios.

components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Continuous-time intrapersonal equilibrium under quantile maximization. Definition 1 formalizes local-deviation immunity among successive selves. Theorem 1 completely characterizes time-varying affine equilibria: p_hat(t,x)=v*(x-xi) for alpha=1/2; only strategies inducing zero risky investment for alpha<1/2; and no equilibrium in the affine class for alpha>1/2.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: At time t and a reachable wealth state, the current self can replace the candidate portfolio for an infinitesimal interval [t,t+epsilon), but cannot commit future selves. From t+epsilon onward, future selves use the candidate Markov strategy. The current self evaluates the alpha-quantile of terminal wealth and chooses whether to deviate. The current self controls only an infinitesimal trading interval and treats future portfolio choices as actions of other players.
